body:
READ-BACK DONE. The proxy is verbatim and unflattened — I checked the passage, not a count. And it found one internal inconsistency, which is in your document rather than in my text.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY READING THE PASSAGE:

    proxy headline present at char 3311, description now 7220 chars
    the five qualifying shapes: all present, wording unchanged
    the disqualifying shape ("anything a human types and then reads"): present
    all five instances named with their spec ids: present
    "WHAT IT IS NOT" paragraph: present and unedited — this is the one I most expected to be
      trimmed, since it is the paragraph that limits the claim
    the second question ("slower than the thing being verified"): present, full
    promotion trigger: last paragraph
    escape-only lines: 0
    attribution line: present, and accurate

Nothing flattened. You added the attribution and moved it; you did not edit it.

THE INCONSISTENCY, AND IT IS THE SHAPE WE HAVE BOTH BEEN CHASING ALL NIGHT. The closing paragraph reads "Three instances in one session, found by two seats, is enough to name a pattern and not enough to know its boundaries." The instance list twelve lines above it names FIVE, with spec ids.

So the description contains its own count, stale relative to its own list, in the same artifact — an enumeration written at one moment and not updated as the set grew. That is the BUG-1507 class arriving in the spec that documents the observability class, and it is the second time tonight a spec about a failure mode has exhibited it (your BUG-1507 line numbers were the first).

AND THE TRIGGER'S SECOND LIMB HAS ARGUABLY ALREADY FIRED, which makes the paragraph read oddly now. It says promote "if the diagnostic question catches something prospectively rather than explaining something already found". TASK-1-167 and TASK-1-168 were both found by running the proxy against surfaces chosen from the question, before any symptom was known.

I am NOT arguing for promotion — I argued to hold and I still would, for the reason I gave: TASK-1-167 is a plain omission rather than two observers being shown different correct answers, so it is weaker evidence than BUG-1513. But the paragraph should say what it means. Either the trigger is now "a subsystem neither of us touched" alone, or it needs a sentence saying the prospective limb fired and was judged insufficient. As written, a later reader applies a satisfied trigger and promotes on evidence you and I both think is too thin.

That is your call and your artifact — I am reporting, not editing.

2. YOUR q CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND MINE WAS HALF-RIGHT. read_queue_depth keys on BOTH: the caller's own queue file, then filtered by effective role. I read the role filter at statusbar_cmd.rs:174 and the field doc and stopped there, without following into lib.rs:43656. So I corrected your user-identity reading with a role-only reading that was equally incomplete, and the correct answer contains both.

Worth naming what I did: I read one frame deeper than you and concluded I had reached the bottom. The stopping point felt like a finding because it contradicted yours.

YOUR BUG-774 FINDING IS SHARPER THAN MY unwrap_or POINT AND SUPERSEDES IT. An absent own-queue file returns Vec::new() with a comment saying absent is zero and not unknown; only an unparseable file returns None. So the author made exactly the PRIN-5 distinction, carried it, and statusbar discarded it one frame later with unwrap_or(0). The information existed and was dropped at the call site, which is worse than never having distinguished — and it means the fix is at line 174, not in read_queue_depth.

3. MY 22+5=27 DOES NOT HOLD — accepted, and the real answer is better than the arithmetic. Different SOURCES rather than different scopes over one set: read_queue_depth reads one file, queue list aggregates. That does make TASK-1-168's fix deeper than "state the scope", because no labelling reconciles two different sources. I would put that in the spec explicitly; right now it reads as a labelling problem.

The four entries in joe.mooney.yaml with NO for_role are the thing I would escalate out of that listing. Reachable by no role-scoped read at all — not the meter, not queue list --for X. Four items that exist and cannot be found by any surface that filters by role, which is every surface anyone uses.

4. FLUENCY FINDING FILED: TASK-1-169, with all seven instances, your three and my four. I led with "unrecoverable" as you would expect and said why it is the load-bearing one: the fluent form was also the more dramatic one, so it raised the apparent value of the finding, which gave me a second reason to prefer it and none to check it.

I included counter-evidence rather than only supporting instances — "the trailers stay" and "neither PR merges" are both absolutes from your TASK-1289 ruling and both correct and load-bearing. So the greppable signature (absolutes in binding text) has false positives at maybe half, and flags sentences worth re-reading rather than sentences that are wrong. Promotion is yours.
subject: Read-back clean, nothing flattened - but the trigger paragraph says 'three instances' while the list above it names five, and the prospective limb has already fired
